content.title: About
content.content: Black beans with meat is a classic Latin American dish consisting of simmered black beans combined with chunks of beef or pork, aromatic spices, and vegetables. The beans provide a rich source of protein and fiber, while the meat adds a hearty flavor and extra iron.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black beans (Phaseolus vulgaris) originated in South America and have been cultivated for centuries.
The dish is often served with rice, corn tortillas, or avocado in many countries.
In Mexico it is known as "frijoles con carne" and is a staple of home cooking.
Black beans contain anthocyanins, giving them their deep color and antioxidant properties.
Traditional recipes include onion, garlic, tomato paste, cumin, and oregano.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Black beans provide about 8 g of protein per 100 g, making them an excellent protein source for vegetarians; meat adds additional high‑quality protein.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: Combined beans and meat deliver easily absorbable iron and zinc, essential for immune function and energy production.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Anthocyanins in black beans have anti‑inflammatory effects and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Beans raise blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for blood‑sugar management.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans, ranging from mild skin symptoms to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned beans often contain added salt; cooking from dry beans allows better control of sodium levels.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Beans can cause gas; proper soaking and thorough cooking reduce this effect.

items.title: Meat quality
items.content: Using fatty cuts increases calorie and saturated fat intake; choose lean cuts if desired.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, typically alongside boiled rice, corn tortillas, or fresh vegetables. A squeeze of lime, chopped cilantro, and a dollop of sour cream brighten the flavor. Leftovers store well in the refrigerator and can be reheated on the stove or in a microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked black beans with meat in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. For longer keeping, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 3 months. Reheat to at least 75 °C before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Toasted sweet potato bread is a whole‑grain loaf that incorporates grated sweet potato and spices into the dough, then slices are toasted until golden and crisp. The sweet potato adds a gentle sweetness, while toasting enhances aroma and creates a crunchy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potato is rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Toasting triggers the Maillard reaction, intensifying flavor through sugars and amino acids.
These breads are common in North American and European cuisines as a quick breakfast or snack.
Sweet potato contains more fiber than regular potato due to its dense structure.
The addition of sweet potato extends shelf life compared with plain bread, as natural sugars inhibit mold growth.

items.title: High in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene supports vision and immune function by converting to vitamin A.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Sweet potato provides slow‑release energy, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole‑grain bread supplies B1, B3, and B6, essential for metabolism.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Makes it suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten intolerance should avoid this product.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet potato raises overall sugar levels, so diabetics should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The added sweet potato makes the loaf more calorie‑dense than plain bread; moderation is key.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted sweet potato bread works well for breakfast with avocado, as a base for sandwiches, in soups, or as a side to salads. Cube it for a crunchy addition to grain bowls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 7 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Discard if mold or off‑odors appear.

chicken-wing-fried-coated-from-pre-cooke.title: Chicken wing, fried, coated, from pre‑cooked product

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken wings are small sections of a bird’s wing that are deep‑fried and coated with a breading. In this case they are taken from a pre‑cooked (pre‑prepared) product, which speeds up preparation and ensures consistent flavor and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are a popular bar and fast‑food snack worldwide.
The coating often consists of flour, spices and breadcrumbs, giving a crispy crust.
The pre‑cooked product (865) can be stored frozen for up to 12 months without quality loss.
In the United States, “Buffalo wings” – wings tossed in a spicy sauce – are a classic.
Wings contain more fat than chicken breast because of the skin and cooking method.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Chicken wings provide about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Wings supply phosphorus and selenium, essential for bone health and antioxidant protection.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying raises the calorie count to roughly 300 kcal per 100 g, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: The breading often contains salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Although rare, a chicken allergy can occur and requires avoidance of the product.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat wings in the oven or microwave and serve with sauces such as barbecue, ranch or hot sauce. They are convenient to eat by hand as a snack and can be added to salads, tacos or rice dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen wings at –18 °C in an airtight package. After thawing, cook immediately and do not store more than 2 days in the refrigerator. Discard if a sour smell or discoloration appears.

content.title: About
content.content: Cranberry juice drink is a refreshing non‑alcoholic beverage made from concentrated cranberry juice, water and a small amount of sugar. It is rich in vitamin C, has a light, slightly tart‑sweet flavor and is suitable for daily consumption or as a complement to meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cranberries contain over 4 mg of vitamin C per 100 g, nearly twice the amount found in oranges.
Traditionally, cranberry juice has been used in North America as a preventive measure against urinary tract infections.
Cranberries are high in antioxidants, including proanthocyanidins, which help combat free radicals.
In Russia, cranberry drinks are often enjoyed during the winter months as a source of vitamins in cold weather.
The natural bright red color of cranberry juice is retained when properly pasteurized.

items.title: High vitamin C content
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis and improves iron absorption.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Cranberry flavonoids help neutralize free radicals, reducing oxidative stress.

items.title: Urinary tract health
items.content: Proanthocyanidins may prevent bacteria from adhering to the walls of the urinary bladder.

items.title: Low‑calorie beverage
items.content: One serving (250 ml) contains about 30 kcal, making it suitable for diet‑friendly nutrition.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The water content helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Despite its low calorie count, the drink contains added sugar, which may be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature of the beverage can cause discomfort for individuals with acid sensitivity or gastritis.

items.title: Cranberry allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cranberries.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve the cranberry drink chilled, use it in cocktails, mix with water or other juices, and pair it with breakfast, desserts or sports activities.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Safflower oil is extracted from the seeds of the safflower plant (Carthamus tinctorius). It is light‑yellow, has a mild nutty aroma, and is rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids, especially linoleic acid (omega‑6). It is widely used in cooking, cosmetics, and the food industry.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Safflower is cultivated in dry regions, notably Russia, India, and the United States.
The seeds contain up to 80 % linoleic acid, making the oil one of the richest sources of this fatty acid.
In the early 20th century, safflower oil was used as a cheaper alternative to more expensive vegetable oils.
Because of its bright yellow hue, safflower oil is sometimes called “sun oil.”
In cosmetics, it is valued for its ability to improve the skin’s barrier function.

items.title: Rich in polyunsaturated fats
items.content: Linoleic acid helps maintain normal blood cholesterol levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports skin health
items.content: The oil moisturizes the epidermis, speeds up healing of minor wounds, and reduces inflammation.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory potential
items.content: Omega‑6 fatty acids can help reduce inflammatory processes when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Immune system support
items.content: Antioxidants and fatty acids contribute to normal immune function.

items.title: High omega‑6 content
items.content: Excessive intake without adequate omega‑3 balance may promote inflammation.

items.title: Allergy risk
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to safflower oil.

items.title: Not suitable for high‑heat frying
items.content: When overheated, the oil can oxidize and form harmful compounds.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Safflower oil is used in salad dressings, marinades, light sautéing, and baking. In cosmetics it is added to creams, lotions, and facial or hair masks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the oil in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it refrigerated to prevent oxidation. Typical shelf life is 12‑18 months.
